subject: UC3 TLS ACME mTLS OCSP CRL
narrative:
## What this unit claims

§2.3 (lines 184-233) makes two kinds of assertion. Eight **current-state** bullets say a capability exists and works today: rustls TLS 1.2/1.3 + ALPN, a dynamic SNI cert resolver, TLS passthrough, cert hot-reload with validation, ACME HTTP-01 with a TTL challenge store, an OCSP fetcher with retry/stale fallback, an OCSP cache with auto-refresh, a CRL fetcher with delta-CRL framework, three mTLS modes, and one closed runtime-config item. Eight **remaining-work** items (UC3.A-H) each assert a specific deficiency, a location, and a day estimate. The unit's framing sentence is "mostly working; some silent stubs (security risk)."

## What the tree says

At `05c56eb` the code is present, largely as described, and better written than the roadmap implies in places. What the roadmap does not say anywhere is that **four of the ten current-state bullets describe subsystems with no production caller at all**. The pattern is uniform: the module is `pub`, unit-tested, re-exported from `src/tls/mod.rs`, and constructed nowhere except its own `#[cfg(test)]` block.

- `AutoHttpsManager` — the only thing that ever constructs an `AcmeClient` — is constructed only at `auto_https.rs:370,384,398,411,421`, all inside its own tests. Zero production callers repo-wide.
- The `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` route exists (`proxy/handler.rs:669-672`) and reads `Option<ChallengeStore>`. `Handler::new` hard-codes that argument to `None` (`handler.rs:145`), and `proxy/server.rs:35` is the only construction site. This is the textbook "present, called, and disabled" shape: the route is reached on every request and can never return a challenge.
- `CertificateReloader` (`cert_reloader.rs:19`) — same, tests only. The shipped startup path is `proxy/server.rs:110` → `TlsManager::load_manual_certificates` (`manager.rs:48-73`), which `std::fs::read`s the PEM and stores it **without validation**. `CertificateValidator::validate` is called from exactly one place, `manager.rs:93`, inside `reload_certificate`, which only the unwired reloader calls.
- `CrlChecker` — tests only, and its delta-CRL branch (`crl_checker.rs:413-415`) is additionally unreachable because `extract_delta_crl_url` is a `TODO` returning `None`.
- `extract_sni` / `passthrough_tls` (`passthrough.rs:20,156`) have no caller outside the module, though `TlsPassthroughConfig` and a DSL directive for it are both parsed.

TLS termination itself **is** wired (`proxy/server.rs:105-135`), so claims 1, 2 and 9 stand on real production code.

The tree also refutes the roadmap in the opposite direction three times. `AcmeConfig` already carries `directory_url`, `staging`, and an `effective_directory_url()` that maps provider+staging onto the Let's Encrypt staging URL (`config/schema.rs:1212-1261`) — UC3.G asks for a field that exists. `AutoHttpsManager` already implements the notBefore/notAfter renewal check UC3.C asks for (`auto_https.rs:98-138`), parsing validity with `x509-parser` and comparing against `renewal_days`. And `manager.rs:242` installs the **external** `ocsp-stapler` 0.4.7 crate (a real dependency, `Cargo.toml:41`, `Cargo.lock:4083`) on the no-mTLS-config branch — which is not the same object as the in-house no-op `crate::tls::ocsp_stapler::Stapler` used on the other two branches. UC3.B's "stapling not wired" is true of two branches out of three.

Two further switched-off findings the document does not mention: `effective_directory_url()` has **zero callers** (`acme.rs:54` reads the raw `directory_url`, and `main.rs:457` sets it to `""`), so `staging: true` does nothing; and `TlsConfig.min_version` (`schema.rs:1183`) is set by every default config and read by no TLS builder, so "TLS 1.2/1.3" holds only as the rustls 0.23 default.

Every citation in the unit omits the crate directory: paths are `src/tls/...` but the workspace member is `highper-gateway/`, so the real path is `highper-gateway/src/tls/...`. The `cargo fmt --all` in `3d18c8c` touched 22 files under `src/tls` (manager.rs +134/-… lines rewrapped), which is why the manager and acme line numbers no longer land.

## Ranked, by how badly each misleads a planner

1. **ACME HTTP-01 listed as current state (line 195).** A planner reads §2.3 and budgets ~1 day for UC3.C to make renewal work. In fact nothing in the shipped binary ever requests or renews a certificate: no `AutoHttpsManager`, no challenge store, `tls.auto` read by nothing. Wiring the ACME lifecycle is unscoped work that appears nowhere in this unit.
2. **UC3.C's diagnosis and its ~1 day estimate (lines 217-220).** The stub it points at has no callers; the working implementation it asks for already exists next door. Someone could spend a day writing code that changes nothing observable.
3. **Cert hot-reload with validation (line 193).** The security-relevant half — validating a certificate before it is trusted — is exactly the half that is not on the production path. The startup path validates nothing.
4. **CRL fetcher (line 201) and TLS passthrough (line 191) as current state.** 808 and 211 lines respectively, fully tested, reachable from nothing.
5. **UC3.G and UC3.F as open work (lines 225-227).** Both are already satisfied or were never true; UC3.G's real defect (the `staging` flag is inert because `effective_directory_url()` is never called) is not what the item asks for.
6. **Stale line numbers** — manager.rs ALPN and resolver, acme.rs `needs_renewal`, commit `fef5bb4`. Cheap to recover from, ranked last.

## Open questions — undocumented choices, not defects

- Why does `manager.rs` use two different staplers? The external `ocsp-stapler` crate on the `mtls: None` branch and the in-house no-op on both `mtls: Some(_)` branches. Nothing records whether that is intentional or a half-finished migration; if it is a migration, UC3.A and UC3.B may be mostly deletion work rather than the ~7 days budgeted.
- `TlsConfig.min_version` and `TlsConfig.auto` are in the schema, set by `main.rs`, and read by nothing. No note says whether they are reserved or abandoned.
- `runtime_config/sections/tls.rs` defines a second `min_version` with its own env var; its relationship to the schema field is unrecorded.

## What I could not check, and why

- **Effort estimates.** ~5d/~2d/~1d/etc. are not observable from a checkout; recorded as one UNVERIFIABLE row.
- **Compilation and CI.** I did not build; running cargo would write to `target/`. The reachability findings come from exhaustive `grep` for construction sites across `highper-gateway/src`, `tests`, `examples` and `xtask`, not from dead-code analysis, so a caller reached only through a trait object or macro would be missed — I saw no such indirection in these paths.
- **`TlsPassthroughConfig` consumption in `proxy/`, `tcp/` and `main.rs`** — the confirming grep was interrupted. The load-bearing fact (no caller of `extract_sni`/`passthrough_tls` outside `passthrough.rs`) is established repo-wide; the weaker statement that the config is parsed and unused rests on the DSL/schema hits only.
- **Other units.** I audited only §2.3 (lines 184-233). §2.4 UC4 and everything else in the file is untouched by this census entry. `SecretRef` was checked only far enough to confirm the §3.6 dependency statement.

claims.claim: Current state: mostly working; some silent stubs (security risk).
claims.note: Not stubs but unreachability: AutoHttpsManager, CertificateReloader, CrlChecker and passthrough::extract_sni are constructed/called only from their own #[cfg(test)] blocks. Four of ten current-state bullets describe code no shipped path runs. 'Mostly working' is true of TLS termination and mTLS only.

claims.claim: rustls TLS 1.2/1.3 with ALPN (`src/tls/manager.rs:244-248`).
claims.note: ALPN (h2, http/1.1) is set at 253-257, not 244-248; cargo fmt 3d18c8c rewrote 134 lines of this file. 1.2+1.3 hold only as rustls 0.23 defaults (Cargo.toml:37 keeps default features incl. tls12); the configured TlsConfig.min_version (config/schema.rs:1183) is read by no TLS builder. Doc paths also omit the crate dir 'highper-gateway/'.

claims.claim: Dynamic `CertResolver` for SNI-based selection (`src/tls/manager.rs:179-318`).
claims.note: DynamicCertResolver is declared at 266-270 and its ResolvesServerCert::resolve at 278-334; line 179 is now MtlsClientVerifier::new. Substance holds and is production-reachable: installed on all three branches of build_server_config, reached from proxy/server.rs:115.

claims.claim: TLS passthrough parses ClientHello SNI (`src/tls/passthrough.rs:20-186`).
claims.note: The cited range is exact (extract_sni 20-52, parse_client_hello 55-124, parse_sni_extension 127-153, passthrough_tls 156-186; tests start 188) and the parser is real. But neither extract_sni nor passthrough_tls has any caller outside this module, so listing it as working current state overstates it: no connection is ever routed through SNI passthrough.

claims.claim: Cert hot-reload with validation (`src/tls/cert_reloader.rs`, `src/tls/cert_validator.rs`).
claims.note: CertificateReloader (19) and start_watching (41) are constructed only in this file's tests (182, 192) — zero production callers. The shipped startup path proxy/server.rs:110 calls load_manual_certificates (manager.rs:48-73), which std::fs::reads and stores PEM with NO validation. CertificateValidator::validate is invoked only at manager.rs:93 inside reload_certificate, reachable only from the unwired reloader.

claims.claim: ACME HTTP-01 challenge with TTL store (`src/tls/acme.rs:95-124`, `src/tls/challenge.rs:19-113`).
claims.note: Both spans are substantively right (challenge handling acme.rs:93-135; ChallengeStore with 1h TTL challenge.rs:19-112). But the capability is switched off: AcmeClient is constructed only by AutoHttpsManager (auto_https.rs:144,162), which is itself constructed only in its own tests; Handler::new hard-codes challenge_store to None (handler.rs:145) and proxy/server.rs:35 is the only construction site, so the /.well-known/acme-challenge/ route (handler.rs:669-672) can never answer. main.rs:451-473 --tls builds an AcmeConfig that only selects a storage dir (manager.rs:26-33).

claims.claim: OCSP fetcher with retry/backoff and stale fallback (`src/tls/ocsp_fetcher.rs:86-277`).
claims.note: Real: fetch_ocsp_response 147-212 (multi-responder), fetch_with_retry 214-254 (exponential backoff, capped), stale fallback branch 200-209 with get_stale_response 300-315. Cited range 86-277 still contains the retry logic but starts in the Default impl and ends before the stale helpers. Reachable only when config.ocsp_stapling.enabled (schema.rs:1509 defaults false), and any live fetch sends the empty body of UC3.A.

claims.claim: OCSP cache with auto-refresh (`src/tls/ocsp_cache.rs:45-165`).
claims.note: start_auto_refresh at 98-123 spawns an interval task; refresh at 128-166; get_response 76. Cited range contains both. Instantiated from the in-house Stapler (ocsp_stapler.rs:76-85), i.e. only on the two mtls-configured branches of build_server_config.

claims.claim: CRL fetcher with delta-CRL framework (`src/tls/crl_checker.rs`).
claims.note: 808 lines with fetch/retry/LRU/is_revoked (263) and apply_delta_crl (598) all present, but CrlChecker is constructed only at 716, 736, 744, 790 — all its own tests. No production caller anywhere in the repo, so no client certificate is ever CRL-checked. The delta branch (413-415) is doubly unreachable: extract_delta_crl_url always returns None.

claims.claim: Three mTLS modes (Required / Optional / OptionalNoCA) at `src/tls/client_verifier.rs:214-250`.
claims.note: Location is still exact (fmt touched this file by 3 lines). OptionalNoCA short-circuits at 233-238; Required vs Optional is decided by client_auth_mandatory at 298-301. Production-reachable via manager.rs:179-182 → proxy/server.rs:115.

claims.claim: `HIGHPER_TLS_CERT_WATCHER_CHANNEL_CAPACITY` bounded channel.
claims.note: Env var parsed at sections/tls.rs:73; cert_watcher.rs:57-62 reads it via try_current() with a default of 32 and builds mpsc::channel(capacity.max(1)) rather than unbounded_channel. Caveat: CertWatcher itself has no production caller (only cert_reloader.rs, which is unwired).

claims.claim: This was B11.1, closed 2026-05-03 in commit `fef5bb4`.
claims.evidence: git commit 2ab3586 (2026-05-03) 'runtime_config: B11.1 - bound cert_watcher unbounded_channel (1 of 5 sites)'
claims.note: `fef5bb4` resolves to no object in this repository (git log --all finds nothing). The work and the date are right; the SHA is not. The same wrong SHA is carried in docs/planning/archive/2026-05-16-v1/ROADMAP_v1.md:3252, so it was copied forward rather than re-derived.

claims.claim: UC3.A — `src/tls/ocsp_fetcher.rs:346-415` never builds a real OCSP request body.
claims.note: build_ocsp_request (357-394) parses the serial, discards it with `let _ = serial;`, warns 'Using simplified OCSP request', and returns Ok(vec![]) at 393. validate_ocsp_response (408-426) checks only non-empty and len >= 10. Cited range still contains both. Note the crate already depends on ocsp-stapler 0.4.7, which the doc's suggested rust-ocsp/webpki-ocsp work may duplicate.

claims.claim: UC3.B — `src/tls/ocsp_stapler.rs:97-136` never attaches cached responses into `CertifiedKey.ocsp` in rustls.
claims.note: attach_ocsp_response (95-137) fetches from cache, logs 'stapling support pending' (125-128) and returns the original certified_key unchanged at 136. resolve (142-166) never even calls it — it returns the inner resolver's key directly. So it is worse than 'never attaches': the attach path is itself dead.

claims.claim: UC3.B is remaining work — OCSP stapling is not wired (~2 days).
claims.note: On the branch where config.mtls is None, manager.rs:242 installs `ocsp_stapler::Stapler::new(cert_resolver)` — one argument, unqualified path, resolving to the EXTERNAL ocsp-stapler crate (Cargo.toml:41, Cargo.lock:4083 v0.4.7), not the in-house crate::tls::ocsp_stapler used at 198 and 222 with two arguments. One of three production paths therefore already delegates stapling to a library that does it.

claims.claim: UC3.C — `src/tls/acme.rs:199-204` `needs_renewal()` always returns `false`.
claims.note: True but moved: AcmeClient::needs_renewal is now 205-209 ('For now, always return false' / Ok(false)); the cited 199-204 ends at the doc comment. fmt 3d18c8c shifted acme.rs by 5 lines.

claims.claim: UC3.C — ACME certs silently never renew; implementing notBefore/notAfter is ~1 day and the highest user-facing severity in §2.3.
claims.note: The asked-for implementation already exists: days_until_expiry (98-118) parses the cert with x509-parser and needs_renewal (121-138) compares it against config.renewal_days, driven by renewal_loop (251-272) via ensure_certificate (204). The acme.rs stub has zero callers repo-wide. Certs do never renew — but because AutoHttpsManager is never constructed outside tests, not because of the stub; fixing the stub as scoped would change nothing.

claims.claim: UC3.D — CRL extension parsers `extract_crl_number` + `extract_delta_crl_url` still to be written via `x509-parser`.
claims.note: extract_crl_number (578-585) and extract_delta_crl_url (588-595) both ignore their argument and return None behind TODOs naming OID 2.5.29.20 and 2.5.29.46. x509-parser 0.16 is already a dependency (Cargo.toml:143), so the item is smaller than it reads — but the containing CrlChecker still has no production caller.

claims.claim: UC3.E — TLS load paths still use blocking `fs::read` and need `tokio::fs::read`.
claims.note: Seven blocking std::fs calls in src/tls and no tokio::fs anywhere in the module. manager.rs:55/59 sit on the production startup path (proxy/server.rs:110), so this one is genuinely open and genuinely on a live path.

claims.claim: UC3.F — Strip ACME private-key PEM from debug logs.
claims.note: No log statement in the crate emits private-key PEM: key_pem/serialize_pem/KeyPair appear in no tracing macro, and although Certificate (storage.rs:12-20) derives Debug over key_pem it is never formatted with {:?}. The nearest match is acme.rs:103-107, which info!-logs the HTTP-01 key AUTHORIZATION (token.thumbprint, served publicly by design) — likely the origin of the item via the 'key_auth=' label.

claims.claim: UC3.G — a TLS staging-URL config field (e.g. `acme.directory_url`) plus an example config are still needed.
claims.note: acme.directory_url (1212-1214) and acme.staging (1216-1218) already exist, plus effective_directory_url() (1243-1261) mapping letsencrypt/zerossl/buypass x staging onto the right directory URL. The real defect, unmentioned: effective_directory_url() has ZERO callers — acme.rs:54 reads the raw directory_url, and main.rs:457 sets it to "" with staging:false, so the staging flag is inert. Example configs (examples/http3-config.yaml:64, highper-gateway/examples/configs/yaml/http3-edge-server.yaml:55) show only the production URL.

claims.claim: UC3.H — a Let's Encrypt staging CI integration test is still needed.
claims.note: No acme/letsencrypt/staging-v02 reference in any workflow or in highper-gateway/tests (only two load-test markdown files mention ACME). The single ACME test, acme.rs:225-248, is #[ignore]d and its assertions are commented out, so it asserts nothing even when run.

claims.claim: Dependencies inherited: §3.6 `SecretRef::Secrets://` resolver, wanted for ACME EAB credentials and OCSP private key access.
claims.note: SecretRef::Secrets { uri, lazy } exists as a parse-only variant whose doc comment states resolve_eager returns 'not implemented' until Phase 1.4, so the dependency is real and unmet. Nothing in src/tls references SecretRef, and acme.rs has no external-account-binding support at all, so the EAB half has no call site waiting for it.

claims.claim: The eight UC3 items cost ~5d (A), ~2d (B), ~1d (C), ~2d (D), ~1/2d (E), ~1/2d (F), ~1/2d (G), ~2d (H).
claims.note: Effort estimates cannot be checked against a checkout — no velocity record, no comparable closed item with a recorded actual, in this repository. Recorded rather than graded. The tree does undermine three of the eight inputs (C and G are largely implemented, F appears not to exist), so the totals rest on premises this audit found false.
